stages.title: Reading and writing fundamentals
stages.hook: In Greek the two letters ου make one sound. Can you guess which one?
explain: Some pairs of letters make one sound: ου sounds like "oo" in "moon", μπ sounds like b, ντ sounds like d, and γκ sounds like g. So σχολείο (school) is said "skholío" and μπαμπάς (dad) is said "bambás".

The stress falls on one of the last three syllables, and the accent mark shows it. Capital letters keep the accent mark in front of a lower-case start, as in Άννα, but all-capital words are written without accents: ΑΘΗΝΑ. Two dots on a vowel, as in παϊδάκι, show that two vowels are read separately.
stages.mnemonic: Two letters, one sound: ου is oo, μπ is b.
sentences: The teacher writes on the board.

gq.q: How is the pair ου pronounced?
gq.why: Greek ου is a single sound, "oo".

gq.q: Where can the stress of a Greek word fall?
o: On one of the last three syllables
gq.why: Greek stress is limited to the last three syllables.

panel.q: How is the sound "b" written in a native-looking Greek word like μπαμπάς?
panel.why: Greek β is v, so μπ is used for b.

panel.q: Why is Άννα written with the mark before the letter?
o: On a capital vowel the accent is written in front of the letter
panel.why: Monotonic spelling puts the accent before a capital vowel.

panel.q: What do two dots on a vowel, as in παϊδάκι, tell the reader?
o: The two vowels are pronounced separately
panel.why: The diaeresis breaks a vowel pair: pa-i.

teach.model: Some pairs of letters make one sound, like ου for "oo", μπ for b and ντ for d. The stress is on one of the last three syllables and the accent mark shows it.

points.ask: Do pairs of letters make one sound?
Can you give me an example word?

trip.prompt: Find the table of letter pairs and read three words aloud.

stages.title: Basic sentence construction
stages.hook: How do you say "but" and "because" so a sentence has two ideas in it?
explain: A Greek sentence has a subject, a verb and often an object. The subject can be left out, as in Μένω εδώ (I live here). Join ideas with και (and), αλλά (but) and γιατί (because).

Γιατί means both "why" in a question and "because" in an answer. Make a verb negative with δεν before it: Δεν ξέρω (I do not know). Use όχι to negate other words: όχι τσάι, καφέ (not tea, but coffee).
stages.mnemonic: Δεν is the little door-closer before a verb.
sentences: Mum is at home and dad works.
I like tea but not coffee.

gq.q: Where does δεν go to make a verb negative?
o: At the end of the sentence
gq.why: Δεν stands directly before the verb.

gq.q: What does γιατί mean in a question?
gq.why: Γιατί asks the reason and also answers it as "because".

panel.q: Why can Greek drop the subject pronoun in Μένω εδώ?
o: There is no subject in Greek
panel.why: Verb endings carry the person.

panel.q: Which word fits: Θέλω τσάι, ___ δεν έχω ζάχαρη?
panel.why: Αλλά introduces a contrast.

panel.q: Why is Δεν ξέρω τίποτα correct although it has two negative words?
panel.why: Τίποτα (nothing) keeps δεν in the clause.

teach.model: A Greek sentence has a verb, and the subject can be dropped. Join ideas with και, αλλά and γιατί. Make a verb negative with δεν before it.

points.ask: How do I say no to a verb?

trip.prompt: Find a negative sentence and mark the word δεν.

stages.title: Common verbs
stages.hook: To say "I want to drink water" Greek does not use an infinitive. How is it done?
explain: Useful verbs are είμαι (I am), έχω (I have), πηγαίνω (I go), κάνω (I do or make), θέλω (I want), μπορώ (I can), ξέρω (I know), μένω (I live, stay). The verb είμαι is irregular: είμαι, είσαι, είναι, είμαστε, είστε, είναι.
Modern Greek has no infinitive. After θέλω or μπορώ we use να and a verb that agrees with the subject: Θέλω να πιω νερό (I want to drink water). The word να means "that" or "to".
sentences: I want a glass of water.

gq.q: Which sentence means "I want to drink water"?
gq.why: After θέλω use να and a verb with the right ending.
Είσαι is the second person singular of είμαι.

panel.q: Why does Modern Greek say θέλω να πιω and not an infinitive?
o: The infinitive disappeared and να plus a finite verb replaces it
panel.why: A finite verb after να agrees with the subject.

panel.q: In Μπορώ να έρθω, what does μπορώ mean?
panel.why: Μπορώ means I can or I am able.

panel.q: Which verb is irregular in Greek?
panel.why: Είμαι has its own set of endings.

teach.model: Use είμαι, έχω, κάνω, θέλω, μπορώ, ξέρω and μένω. Greek has no infinitive, so say θέλω να πιω νερό: θέλω, να, and a verb with the right ending.

points.ask: How do I say I want to drink?

trip.prompt: Find the forms of είμαι and say them in order.

stages.title: Nouns, pronouns and modifiers
stages.hook: In Greek the adjective changes ending with the noun. Which ending goes with a house, το σπίτι?
explain: Pronouns: εγώ, εσύ, αυτός, αυτή, αυτό, εμείς, εσείς, αυτοί. Because verb endings show the person, subject pronouns are used mostly for emphasis.

Adjectives agree with the noun in gender, number and case: ο μεγάλος δρόμος, η μεγάλη πόλη, το μεγάλο σπίτι. The article is repeated before the adjective. "Our" is μας and follows the noun: η πόλη μας.
stages.mnemonic: Big man, big city, big house: μεγάλος, μεγάλη, μεγάλο.

gq.why: Πόλη is feminine, so the adjective takes -η.

o: After the noun: η πόλη μας
Before the noun: μας η πόλη
At the end of the sentence
gq.why: The weak possessive follows the noun.

panel.q: Why do Greeks usually not say εγώ with verbs?
o: The verb ending already shows the person
panel.why: Pronouns are used for emphasis.

panel.q: Why is it το μεγάλο σπίτι with two neuter forms?
o: The article and adjective both agree with the neuter noun
panel.why: Article, adjective and noun share gender, number and case.

panel.q: Which pronoun fits for a group of men?
panel.why: Αυτοί is masculine plural.

teach.model: Greek pronouns are εγώ, εσύ, αυτός, αυτή, αυτό, εμείς, εσείς, αυτοί, mainly used for emphasis. Adjectives match the noun and the article is repeated: το μεγάλο σπίτι.

trip.prompt: Find the adjective table for μεγάλος and read the forms aloud.

stages.title: Questions and responses
stages.hook: In Greece a quick upward head tilt can mean "no". What can you say with words?
explain: Question words are ποιος (who), τι (what), πού (where), πότε (when), γιατί (why), πώς (how), πόσο (how much) and ποιο (which). Note the accent: πού is a question word, while που without an accent means "that" or "who" inside a sentence.

A yes/no question has the same words as a statement and a rising voice. Reply with Ναι, μου αρέσει or Όχι, δεν μου αρέσει. A quick upward tilt of the head, sometimes with a click, often means "no" in Greece, so watch for gestures.
stages.mnemonic: Πού with an accent asks a question; που alone just joins.

gq.q: What does the accent show in πού?
gq.why: Without an accent που links clauses.

gq.q: A friend tilts the head up quickly. What can this mean in Greece?
gq.why: The upward head tilt often means no.

panel.q: Why is Δεν ξέρω τίποτα correct?
panel.why: Δεν plus τίποτα is standard.

panel.q: How do you form a yes/no question aloud?
panel.why: The words stay the same.

panel.q: Why is πώς with the accent different from πως?
o: Πώς means how in questions, while πως means "that"
panel.why: The accent separates the two words.

teach.model: Use ποιος, τι, πού, πότε, γιατί, πώς and πόσο. Yes/no questions use rising voice and the Greek question mark ;. The accent in πού and πώς shows a question.

points.ask: How do I ask a yes/no question?

trip.prompt: Find the part about gestures in Greece and note one more.

stages.title: Describing people and places
stages.hook: To say "in the village" Greek joins two words into one. Which two?
explain: Describing words: ψηλός (tall), καλός (kind, good), χαρούμενος (cheerful), όμορφος (beautiful), καινούργιος (new), παλιός (old). They change with gender: ο αδελφός μου είναι ψηλός, η αδελφή μου είναι ψηλή.
For places use σε (in, at, to). It joins with the article: σε + το = στο, σε + την = στην. So στο χωριό (in the village), στην πόλη (in the city).
stages.mnemonic: Σε + το = στο: two words, one hug.
sentences: It is quiet in the village.

gq.q: How do you say "My sister is tall"?
gq.why: The adjective takes the feminine ending.

panel.q: Why is it στο and not σε το?
panel.why: Σε contracts with the article.

panel.q: Why do adjectives like όμορφος have three forms?
o: They agree with masculine, feminine and neuter nouns
panel.why: Όμορφος, όμορφη, όμορφο.

panel.q: In Στο χωριό είναι ήσυχα, what is ήσυχα?
o: An adverb for how things are
panel.why: It describes the situation, like "quietly".

teach.model: Adjectives change ending: ψηλός, ψηλή, ψηλό. Use σε for places and merge with the article: στο χωριό, στην πόλη.

points.ask: How do I say in the city?

trip.prompt: Find the preposition σε and write two sentences with it.

stages.title: Time, dates and daily routines
stages.hook: In Greek, Tuesday means "third". Can you work out what Monday means?
explain: Time words: μέρα (day), εβδομάδα (week), μήνας (month), χρόνος (year), πρωί (morning), βράδυ (evening). Days: δευτέρα, τρίτη, τετάρτη, πέμπτη, παρασκευή, σάββατο, κυριακή. They are usually written in lower case.

Several names come from ordinals: δευτέρα means "second", τρίτη "third", τετάρτη "fourth", πέμπτη "fifth". Κυριακή is the Lord's day. For clock times say στις επτά (at seven). Ask Τι ώρα είναι; (What time is it?).
stages.mnemonic: Second, third, fourth, fifth: δευτέρα to πέμπτη.
sentences: The lesson starts in the morning.

gq.q: What time do you say for 7 o'clock?
gq.why: For hours after one Greek uses στις, from σε + τις.

panel.q: What does δευτέρα originally mean?
panel.why: Greek counts the week from Sunday, so Monday is second.

panel.q: Why is it στις επτά?
o: Hours are plural and take the feminine plural article
panel.why: Ώρα is feminine, so τις is used for the hours.

panel.q: Which question asks the time?
panel.why: Τι ώρα είναι; is the usual question.

teach.model: Day names come from ordinals: δευτέρα is second, τρίτη third. Say clock time with στις: στις επτά. Ask Τι ώρα είναι;

points.ask: How do I say at seven?
How do I ask the time?

trip.prompt: Find the Greek names and the ordinals they come from.

stages.title: Food and shopping
stages.hook: How do you politely say "I would like" in Greek when ordering something?
explain: Food and shop words: ψωμί (bread), σούπα (soup), μήλο (apple), τυρί (cheese), μαγαζί (shop), τιμή (price), ευρώ (euro). Ask Πόσο κάνει; (How much is it?).
To ask politely say Θα ήθελα (I would like) or use παρακαλώ: Ένα μήλο, παρακαλώ. Greece uses the euro. Traditional hospitality, called φιλοξενία, means welcoming guests warmly.
stages.mnemonic: Θα ήθελα + παρακαλώ: the polite pair.

gq.q: Which phrase is the more polite way to ask?
What currency is used in Greece?
gq.why: Greece adopted the euro in 2001, and notes and coins came in 2002.

panel.q: What does φιλοξενία mean?
panel.why: Philoxenia literally means love of the stranger or guest.

panel.q: Why does μήλο become μήλα for "apples"?
o: Neuter nouns in -ο form their plural with -α
panel.why: Μήλο, μήλα follows the neuter pattern.

panel.q: Why do you say παρακαλώ with a request?
panel.why: Παρακαλώ means please.

teach.model: Ask the price with Πόσο κάνει; Ask politely with Θα ήθελα or παρακαλώ. Greece uses the euro.

points.ask: How do I ask the price?

trip.prompt: Find a traditional dish and read its Greek name aloud.

stages.title: Everyday conversations
stages.hook: Greeks often say "Τα λέμε", which literally means "we say them". What does it really mean?
explain: Useful questions: Από πού είσαι; (Where are you from?), Τι νέα; (What is new?). Answer with Είμαι από τη Γκάνα, Είμαι από τη Νιγηρία. Από is followed by the accusative: από την Ελλάδα.
Say goodbye with Τα λέμε! (See you!) and Καλή μέρα! (Have a good day!). The answer is Επίσης! (You too!). With friends propose Ας βρεθούμε (Let us meet).
stages.mnemonic: Τα λέμε: we will "talk" again soon.

gq.q: What is the polite reply to Καλή μέρα;
What does Τα λέμε usually mean?
gq.why: It is a common friendly goodbye.

panel.q: Which preposition is used for "from" with a country?
panel.why: Από takes the accusative.

panel.q: Why is Τα λέμε not translated word for word?
panel.why: Idioms have a meaning different from the words.

panel.q: In Ας βρεθούμε, what does ας suggest?
panel.why: Ας plus a verb forms an invitation.

teach.model: Ask Από πού είσαι; and answer Είμαι από τη Γκάνα. Say Τα λέμε! for see you and Καλή μέρα! for have a good day. The answer is Επίσης!

points.ask: How do I ask where someone is from?
How do I say see you?
How do I reply to good wishes?

trip.prompt: Find a short dialogue and read it aloud.
